page: Amazon Web Services r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC 7R13 cores running at 3.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mixed profile. Single-core CPU performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25% at 2976.78. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth tests show limitations. Stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores fall into the average range, while memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks are categorized as weak. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks show weak performance, reflecting the constraints of a 4-vCPU configuration. Cryptographic operations perform moderately, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, the r6a.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing or high-speed local storage. It is suited for moderate database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. However, its weak multi-threaded decompression, poor medium-model LLM inference speeds, and weak Redis SET performance make it less suitable for compute-heavy or high-throughput real-time data processing tasks.
